Laura / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick read, Sofia (forwarding for context). I want to align on two things before we send an offer: 1) whether we anchor this as L5 Manager (manager track) vs L5 Senior IC, and 2) the comp structure we can approve without escalating to People Ops.

My assessment: Maria's background includes people management + hiring at Scale, and she explicitly asked for a manager trajectory. The role we scoped originally has roadmap ownership and potential to hire (headcount approval pending). If we intend to give her the ability to hire within 6–9 months, manager title makes sense. If we keep the role as IC with strong technical leadership but no direct reports, we should offer Senior IC and make the manager track a clear promotion path.

Proposed offer (draft for quick review):
- Title: L5 Manager (conditional on headcount signoff in Q4)
- Base: $170,000
- Target bonus: 20%
- Equity: 0.25% (4-year vest, 1y cliff)
- Signing bonus: $15,000 pro-rated if notice extends beyond 2 weeks

Attachments: offer-maria-santiago-v1.pdf (draft)

Ask: Laura — can you confirm whether comp grid allows the above anchor without requiring a People Ops escalation? Marcus — can you confirm we have the headcount runway to convert the role to manager within the proposed timeframe? If either answer is no, I'll pivot to Senior IC language and adjust equity/banding.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

Grace —

Quick thoughts: I agree with your framing. Two operational notes from compensation side:

1) Banding: L5 Manager and L5 Senior IC share the same comp band here, so your proposed base ($170k) is squarely inside the band midpoint for Bay Area remote hires. Equity of 0.25% is reasonable for L5 manager candidates with hiring expectations.

2) Approvals: Anything at or below $175k base and equity <=0.3% can be approved by me (Director-level signoff). If we go above that (or want a higher signing bonus), People Ops + finance need to sign off.

3) Language: If we go manager, include conditional phrasing: "Manager title contingent on headcount approval within 9 months" — keeps us flexible and signals path to the candidate.

I'm okay to approve today for the numbers you listed. Marcus, please confirm runway for converting to a manager role (headcount).

- Laura
VP, Talent and People Ops
